name: Norepinephrine
summary: Norepinephrine (NE), also called noradrenaline (NA) or noradrenalin, is an organic chemical in the catecholamine family that functions in the brain and body as a hormone, neurotransmitter and neuromodulator.

pharmacology.text: A large number of important drugs exert their effects by interacting with norepinephrine systems in the brain or body. Their uses include treatment of cardiovascular problems, shock, and a variety of psychiatric conditions. These drugs are divided into: sympathomimetic drugs which mimic or enhance at least some of the effects of norepinephrine released by the sympathetic nervous system; sympatholytic drugs, in contrast, block at least some of the effects.

uses.text: Regardless of which name is used for the substance itself, parts of the body that produce or are affected by it are referred to as noradrenergic. Outside the brain, norepinephrine is used as a neurotransmitter by sympathetic ganglia located near the spinal cord or in the abdomen, as well as Merkel cells located in the skin.

zhOther: 去甲基腎上腺素, 正腎上腺素, 降腎上腺素
summaryZh: 正腎上腺素又稱去甲腎上腺素，簡稱去甲腎、正腎，是一種兒茶酚胺類生物活性物質，由交感節後神經元、腦內腎上腺能神經元及腎上腺髓質合成和分泌，作為中樞和外周的神經傳導物質，也作為激素。循環血液中的正腎上腺素主要來自腎上腺髓質。

sideEffects.en: Given as a medicine in intensive care it raises blood pressure, and it can cause a slow or irregular heartbeat, anxiety and headache. If it leaks from the vein it can damage the surrounding tissue, and strong narrowing of blood vessels can starve the fingers, toes or gut of blood.
sideEffects.zh: 在加護治療中作為藥物使用時，它會升高血壓，並可能造成心跳過慢或不規則、焦慮與頭痛。若從靜脈滲漏，可能傷害周圍組織；血管強烈收縮時，手指、腳趾或腸道可能缺血。
sideEffects.zhHans: 在加护治疗中作为药物使用时，它会升高血压，并可能造成心跳过慢或不规则、焦虑与头痛。若从静脉渗漏，可能伤害周围组织；血管强烈收缩时，手指、脚趾或肠道可能缺血。

fact.en: Noradrenaline was identified as the body's main sympathetic nerve messenger by the Swedish scientist Ulf von Euler in 1946, work for which he shared a Nobel Prize in 1970.
fact.zh: 瑞典科學家烏爾夫．馮．奧伊勒在 1946 年確認正腎上腺素是人體交感神經的主要傳訊物質，他因相關研究在 1970 年共同獲得諾貝爾獎。
fact.zhHans: 瑞典科学家乌尔夫．冯．奥伊勒在 1946 年确认正肾上腺素是人体交感神经的主要传讯物质，他因相关研究在 1970 年共同获得诺贝尔奖。
